text.en: A bit of Hydra grows into a new animal and a potato eye becomes a new plant. Many organisms reproduce from a single parent.

Reproduction creates new individuals that copy the DNA of the parent, with small variations that help species survive.
Binary fission: Amoeba splits into two, and Plasmodium splits into many in multiple fission.
Fragmentation: Spirogyra breaks into pieces and each grows into a new filament.
Regeneration: Hydra and Planaria regrow lost parts from specialised cells.
Budding: Hydra forms a bud that grows and detaches.
Vegetative propagation: new plants from roots, stems or leaves, as in potato, Bryophyllum and sugarcane. Grafting, cutting and layering help gardeners.
Spore formation: Rhizopus makes spores in sporangia that grow in damp conditions.
Asexual reproduction gives little variation, but it is fast and needs only one parent. Tissue culture grows plants from a few cells in a lab.
